text: Route prefix: /er. Manages emergency patient intake, triage, bed assignment, treatment, OECB billing, and disposition. Core component: ErAdmissionCrud (Livewire, WithPagination).

Route: er.triage (permission: er.triage). Triage records capture the initial patient assessment on arrival. Fields: id, tenant_id, patient_id, er_admission_id (FK, nullable - can exist before admission), acuity_level_id (FK to er_acuity_levels), mobility_status_id (FK to er_mobility_statuses), triage_notes (text), triaged_by (FK to users/HCPs), triage_datetime, status, history, audit columns. Triage is typically the FIRST record created when a patient arrives at the ER.

Route: er.acuity-levels (permission: er.manage). Emergency severity levels: Level 1 - Immediate/Critical (life-threatening, needs immediate intervention), Level 2 - Emergency (potentially life-threatening, needs immediate evaluation), Level 3 - Urgent (serious but stable, needs prompt evaluation), Level 4 - Less Urgent (needs evaluation but not immediately), Level 5 - Non-Urgent (minor issue, can wait). Fields: id, name, code, description, color (for visual triage tagging), is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns.

Route: er.mobility-statuses (permission: er.manage). Patient mobility on arrival: Ambulatory (walking), Wheelchair, Stretcher, Bedridden, Unresponsive. Fields: id, name, code, description, is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns.

Route: er.zones (permission: er.manage). Physical zones in the ER: Red Zone (critical - resuscitation), Yellow Zone (urgent - monitored), Green Zone (less urgent - waiting), etc. Fields: id, name, code, description, color, is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns. Zones group beds.

Route: er.beds (permission: er.manage). Individual ER beds. Each bed belongs to a zone (zone_id FK). Fields: id, zone_id, bed_number, bed_type, status (Available/Occupied/Occupied-Isolation/Maintenance), notes, is_active, tenant_id, history, audit columns. When a bed is assigned to an admission, its status changes to 'Occupied'. When the admission is edited to a different bed or the patient is discharged, the old bed's status is set back to 'Available' (handled in saveEdit method of ErAdmissionCrud).
Route: er.area (permission: er.manage). ER area configuration - broader physical areas that contain zones.

items: id - Primary key.
tenant_id - FK to hospitals.id.
patient_id - FK to patients.id.
admission_code - Code: 'ER#' + id (e.g. ER#1, ER#2). Set as 'ER#' . $id on creation.
er_bed_id - FK to er_beds.id (nullable). Assigned bed.
attending_physician_id - FK to health_care_professionals.id.
initial_diagnosis - String, max 2000. Initial diagnosis on admission.
history_of_present_illness - Text, max 10000. HPI.
physical_exam_findings - Text, max 10000. Physical exam.
assessment - Text, max 10000. Assessment/diagnosis.
orders_summary - Text, max 10000. Summary of orders.
treatment_notes - Text, max 10000. Treatment notes.
is_oecb - Boolean. Whether this admission is billed under OECB (Outpatient Emergency Case Billing).
oecb_entries - JSON array of OECB entries (see 7.3).
mode_of_arrival - String. How the patient arrived: Walk-in, Ambulance, Private Vehicle, Motorcycle, Tricycle, Public Transport, etc.
disposition - String. Outcome: Discharged, Admitted (inpatient), Referred, Left Without Being Seen, Against Medical Advice, Expired, etc.
discharge_instructions - Text. Instructions given to patient on discharge.
admission_datetime - DateTime. When the patient was admitted.
status - Admission status: Pending, In Progress, Discharged, Admitted, Referred, Cancelled, etc.
created_by / created_date - Audit columns.
updated_by / updated_date - Audit columns.
history - Soft delete flag (1=active).
is_active - Active flag.

text: OECB is the Philippine emergency billing system. Each ER admission can be flagged as is_oecb=true, and OECB entries are recorded. From the ErAdmissionCrud source code:

items: core_presentation - String, max 200. The core presentation name (e.g. 'Abdominal Pain', 'Chest Pain', 'Trauma'). Selected from OECB core presentation master.
oecb_package_code - String, max 30. Auto-populated when core_presentation is selected. Looked up from OecbFeeSchedule::whereHas('corePresentation', fn($q) => $q->where('name', $value))->first().
oecb_fixed_fee - Float (nullable). Auto-populated from the fee schedule when core_presentation is selected. The fixed fee for this OECB package.
Each OECB entry is stored in the oecb_entries JSON column on the ErAdmission record.
Toggle is_oecb checkbox on the treatment form to enable OECB entry.
Click 'Add OECB Entry' to add a new entry row.
Type the core_presentation name - the system auto-fetches the package_code and fixed_fee from OecbFeeSchedule.
Multiple OECB entries can be added (e.g. multiple presentations for the same patient).
Click the X on an entry row to remove it (removeOecbEntry method).

On saveTreatment(): OECB entries are synced to the admission record via syncOecbEntries(). Existing entries not in the submitted array are deleted. New entries are inserted. Modified entries are updated.
The EECL PDF (see 7.4) includes all OECB entries with their core presentation, package code, and fixed fee.

text: The OecbFeeSchedule model links core presentations to their package codes and fixed fees. Looked up dynamically when core_presentation is selected in the UI. This is the fee reference for emergency billing.

items: TRIAGE (er.triage permission): Create a triage record. Select patient, acuity level, mobility status, triage notes. Triage record created first - this captures the initial severity assessment.

CREATE ER ADMISSION: From the triage or directly, create an ER admission. Fields: patient_id, er_bed_id (assign a bed from ER > Beds - the bed status changes to 'Occupied'), attending_physician_id, initial_diagnosis, mode_of_arrival, admission_datetime = now(), status = 'Pending'.

BED MANAGEMENT: When editing an admission's bed (saveEdit method): if the bed is changing, the OLD bed's status is set back to 'Available' and the NEW bed's status is set to 'Occupied'. This keeps bed availability accurate in real-time.
TREATMENT (openTreatment + saveTreatment): The treatment form captures the full clinical documentation:
- history_of_present_illness (max 10000)
- physical_exam_findings (max 10000)
- assessment (max 10000)
- orders_summary (max 10000)
- treatment_notes (max 10000)
- is_oecb (toggle)
- oecb_entries (dynamic rows with core_presentation, package_code, fixed_fee)
- disposition (outcome)
- discharge_instructions
On saveTreatment: Updates all fields, syncs OECB entries, uses updated_by/updated_date.

ORDERS: From the ER admission, orders can be placed just like OPD: Lab (LR-), Pharmacy (PR-), CSR (CR-), Radiology (Rad-), Procedures (Proc-). Each order links to the ER admission via er_admission_id and creates the appropriate request/items.

DISPOSITION: Set the final outcome via the disposition field on the treatment form. Options: Discharged (patient goes home), Admitted (patient admitted to inpatient ward/ICU - creates an inpatient admission), Referred (sent to another facility), Left Without Being Seen (patient left before treatment), Against Medical Advice, Expired.
EECL PDF: When is_oecb=true, the EECL PDF becomes available at er.admission.eeclpdf route. See 7.5.

text: Route: er.admission.eeclpdf ({admission}, permission: er.manage). Generates a PDF via DomPDF downloaded as eecl-{admission_code}.pdf. The EECL PDF includes:

items: Patient information (name, age, sex)
PhilHealth member details (if patient has linked PhilHealth membership)
Attending physician name
OECB entries (all core_presentation, package_code, fixed_fee rows) - ONLY if is_oecb=true
Triage record: acuity level name, mobility status, triage notes, triage datetime
ER bed and zone assignment
Admission datetime
Initial diagnosis
Disposition

text: ER orders work identically to OPD orders (see 6.5) but link to er_admission_id instead of opd_consultation_id. The ErAdmissionCrud has order modal fields for:

items: Lab orders: orderLabSelection, orderLabPriority (default 'Urgent'), orderLabNotes
CSR orders: orderCsrSelection, orderCsrQuantities, orderCsrNotes
Radiology orders: orderRadiologySelection, orderRadiologyPriority (default 'Urgent'), orderRadiologyNotes

Pharmacy orders: orderPharmacySelection, orderPharmacyQuantities, orderPharmacyFrequencies (per-drug CF4 frequency like BID, TID, QID, etc.), orderPharmacyRoutes (per-drug CF4 route like PO, IV, IM, SC, etc.), orderPharmacyPriority (default 'Urgent'), orderPharmacyNotes
Procedure orders: orderProcedureSelection, orderProcedureQuantities, orderProcedureNotes
The priority defaults to 'Urgent' for ER (vs 'Routine' for OPD) reflecting the emergency nature.

text: 8. Inpatient Admission, ICU, Ward, and OR

Route: /admission (permission: admission.view). Manages inpatient admissions. This is where patients who need hospitalization are admitted. The admission record links to a ward room or ICU bed, and serves as the anchor for all inpatient orders, billing, and discharge.

items: Admission code: ADM#<id> (e.g. ADM#1, ADM#2).

Key fields: patient_id, admitting_diagnosis, attending_physician_id, admission_type, admission_date, ward_room_id (FK to ward_rooms) OR icu_bed_id (FK to icu_beds), status (Admitted, Discharged, Transfer, Expired, etc.), discharge_date, discharge_disposition, discharge_instructions.
The admission is the central record for an inpatient stay. All orders (lab, pharmacy, CSR, radiology, procedure) link to the admission via admission_id.
When the patient is discharged, the assigned room/bed status is set back to 'Available' and the discharge_date is recorded.
Admission Room History: When a patient is moved between rooms during their stay, the AdmissionRoomHistory model tracks each move with from_room, to_room, moved_by, moved_date for audit trail.

text: Route prefix: /icu (permission: admission.view). Manages critical care beds.

items: ICU > Wards: ICU ward names (e.g. Medical ICU, Surgical ICU, Cardiac ICU). Fields: id, name, code, description, is_active, tenant_id, history.
ICU > Beds: Individual ICU beds. Each bed belongs to an ICU ward (icu_ward_id FK). Fields: id, icu_ward_id, bed_number, bed_type, status (Available/Occupied), is_active, tenant_id, history.
ICU beds are assigned to admissions for critical care patients (icu_bed_id on the Admission model).
When an ICU bed is assigned, its status changes to 'Occupied'. When freed, status returns to 'Available'.

text: Route prefix: /micu (permission: admission.view). Medical (non-surgical) critical care tracking.

items: MICU > Patients: MICU-specific patient records. Tracks patients admitted to the Medical ICU with their MICU-specific data. Fields: id, patient_id, icu_bed_id, admission_id, micu_admission_date, micu_discharge_date, primary_diagnosis, micro_organism (if applicable), micu_status, created_by, created_date, history.

MICU > Assessment Parameters: Critical care assessment data captured for MICU patients. Fields: id, micu_patient_id, assessment_date, vitals (BP, HR, temp, RR, SpO2), laboratory values (ABG, electrolytes, CBC, etc.), severity scores (APACHE II, SOFA, Glasgow Coma Scale), ventilator settings (if applicable), fluid_balance, urine_output, created_by, created_date, history.
Assessment parameters are captured periodically (e.g. every shift or every 4-6 hours) to track the patient's critical care trajectory.

text: Route prefix: /ward (permission: admission.view). Manages general inpatient wards and rooms.

items: Ward > Wards: Ward names (General Ward, Private Ward, Semi-Private, VIP Ward, Pediatric Ward, etc.). Fields: id, name, code, description, bed_capacity, is_active, tenant_id, history.

Ward > Room Types: Room categories (Single Room, Double Room, Quadruple Room, Ward Bed, Semi-Private Room, etc.). Fields: id, name, code, description, bed_count_per_room, rate_per_day (for billing), is_active, tenant_id, history.

Ward > Rooms: Individual rooms. Each room belongs to a ward (ward_id FK) and a room type (room_type_id FK). Fields: id, ward_id, room_type_id, room_number, floor, bed_count, status (Available/Occupied/Full/Maintenance), notes, is_active, tenant_id, history.
Rooms are assigned to admissions (ward_room_id on the Admission model).
When a room is assigned, bed_count is decremented. When the patient is discharged, the bed is freed and bed_count incremented.
Room transfers: tracked in AdmissionRoomHistory for audit.

text: Route prefix: /or (permission: or.view). Manages operating theatre scheduling and rooms.

items: OR > Rooms: Operating room names/codes (OR 1, OR 2, Main OR, Cardiac OR, Neuro OR, etc.). Fields: id, name, code, description, floor, status (Available/Booked/Maintenance), is_active, tenant_id, history.

OR > Schedule: OR procedure scheduling. The OR schedule is created from the ErAdmissionCrud's showOrScheduleModal + the OR scheduling form. Fields: id, patient_id, admission_id (nullable), or_room_id (FK to or_rooms), procedure_type, procedure_description, surgeon_id (FK to health_care_professionals), anesthesiologist_id (FK to health_care_professionals), scheduled_date, start_time, end_time, pre_op_notes, intra_op_notes, post_op_notes, status (Scheduled/In Progress/Completed/Cancelled), created_by, created_date, history.
The OR schedule drives operating theatre utilization. Surgeons and anesthesiologists are both assigned. Pre/intra/post-op notes are captured during the procedure workflow.
OR schedule integrates with the procedure module (procedures are ordered and linked to OR schedule) and billing (OR use is billed).
